title: The Commodity Markets Outlook in eight charts
gist: The World Bank's October 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook projects commodity prices rising 23% in 2026 before falling 7% in 2027, driven by Middle East hostilities, the Strait of Hormuz disruption, Black Sea grain disruptions and a very strong El Niño. Brent is forecast at $91/bbl in 2026, $79 in 2027 and $70 in 2028, with near-term risks tilted to the upside.

insights.claim: The World Bank projects its global commodity price index to rise 23 percent in 2026 before declining 7 percent in 2027.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Commodity-driven inflation pressure persists through 2026 before easing.
insights.quote: Commodity prices are set to remain elevated, with the global index projected to rise 23 percent in 2026 before declining 7 percent in 2027.
insights.locator: Commodity prices are set to remain

insights.claim: Energy and fertilizer price indexes are expected to rise 32 and 14 percent respectively in 2026 before easing in 2027.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Energy and fertilizer are the main 2026 inflation drivers within commodities.
insights.locator: Commodity prices are set to remain

insights.claim: Overall commodity price risks are tilted to the upside, including prolonged Middle East hostilities, stronger El Niño effects and extended Black Sea supply disruptions.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Skew favors upside surprises in commodity prices and related inflation.
insights.locator: Commodity prices are set to remain

insights.claim: Commodity markets were highly volatile through 2026 amid Middle East tensions and disruptions to Black Sea grain supplies, with the World Bank Group food price index reaching a three-year high in September.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Food inflation risk is elevated for import-dependent economies.
insights.locator: Commodity markets were highly volatile

themes.theme: Oil: Hormuz shock now, surplus later

insights.claim: Front-month Brent futures exceeded $110/bbl in mid-October 2026 as hostilities in the Strait of Hormuz constrained flows, even as markets weighed rising crude supply and accelerated IEA emergency stock releases.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Oil is pricing a significant geopolitical risk premium.
insights.locator: Oil prices have been exceptionally volatile

insights.claim: Oil volatility in 2026Q3 was driven by renewed hostilities in the Gulf and Red Sea, an attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline, and intensifying attacks on Russian oil facilities.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Multiple concurrent supply-side shocks underpin energy price risk.
insights.locator: Oil prices have been exceptionally volatile

insights.claim: The World Bank expects Brent to average $91/bbl in 2026, $79/bbl in 2027 and $70/bbl in 2028 as the oil market moves into surplus.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Forecast implies roughly 23% decline from 2026 average to 2028; supports a bearish medium-term oil view.
insights.quote: Brent is expected to average $91/bbl in 2026 before declining to $79/bbl in 2027 and $70/bbl in 2028 as the market moves into surplus.
insights.locator: Oil prices have been exceptionally volatile

insights.claim: Near-term oil risks are tilted to the upside from conflict supply losses and tighter OPEC+ policy amid depleted inventories, while longer-term risks are to the downside from faster Gulf restoration, stronger non-OPEC+ output, weaker growth and faster EV adoption.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Asymmetric risk: upside near term, downside further out, suggesting backwardation-type positioning.
insights.locator: Oil prices have been exceptionally volatile

insights.claim: Refinery damage pushed up petroleum product prices, particularly diesel.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Refining margins, especially diesel cracks, are elevated.
insights.locator: Commodity markets were highly volatile

insights.claim: European and Asian LNG prices more than doubled from pre-conflict levels by September 2026, and the World Bank natural gas index hit a four-year high, amid Gulf supply disruptions, strong Asian power demand and low European inventories.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: European and Asian gas consumers face a severe energy cost shock.
insights.locator: Natural gas prices surged in 2026Q3

insights.claim: U.S. natural gas prices generally remained below their February 2026 levels even as European and Asian prices surged.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Wide transatlantic gas spread favors U.S. LNG exporters and U.S. gas-intensive industry.
insights.locator: Natural gas prices surged in 2026Q3

insights.claim: Global gas markets are expected to stay tight despite a partial Gulf LNG export recovery in 2027Q1, because Qatar's damaged LNG trains are assumed to remain offline.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Qatar's outage is a structural constraint on LNG supply into 2027.
insights.locator: Natural gas prices surged in 2026Q3

insights.claim: European gas prices are projected to rise about 60 percent in 2026, then fall 8 percent in 2027 and almost 30 percent in 2028 as markets normalize.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: European energy-intensive sectors face peak cost pressure in 2026 with relief by 2028.
insights.locator: Natural gas prices surged in 2026Q3

insights.claim: U.S. natural gas prices are expected to be broadly unchanged in 2026 and then rise about 6 percent in 2027 and 5 percent in 2028, largely reflecting growing external demand for LNG.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Export pull gradually tightens the U.S. gas market, supportive for U.S. producers.
insights.locator: Natural gas prices surged in 2026Q3

insights.claim: Food prices are expected to rise 10 percent in 2026 and another 7 percent in 2027, after a 21 percent decline between 2022 and 2025, due to elevated input costs, Black Sea disruptions and El Niño harvest losses.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Food inflation is re-accelerating, a risk to EM inflation and central bank easing.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s agricultural price index

insights.claim: Rice production is expected to fall for the first time in a decade, and palm oil production in Southeast Asia is expected to be constrained.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Supportive for rice and palm oil prices; negative for Asian food importers.
insights.quote: Rice production is expected to fall for the first time in a decade
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s agricultural price index

insights.claim: Trade disruptions and hot, dry conditions in the EU and elsewhere are expected to push wheat prices sharply higher.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Bullish wheat outlook.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s agricultural price index

insights.claim: Beverage prices are projected to fall 24 percent in 2026 as coffee and cocoa production recovers, before rising 3 percent in 2027.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Softs are an exception to the commodity upswing; bearish coffee and cocoa in 2026.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s agricultural price index

insights.claim: Intensified conflict and larger weather losses could push food and grain prices 12 percent and 20 percent above the 2027 baseline, respectively, while export restrictions or pro-biofuel policies could add further pressure.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Quantifies tail risk for grain prices.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s agricultural price index

insights.claim: Increased diversion of crops to biofuels, especially biodiesel, is adding to food price pressure.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Biofuel mandates link vegetable oil prices to energy policy.
insights.locator: Commodity prices are set to remain

insights.claim: The World Bank fertilizer price index fell 22 percent q/q in 2026Q3 and further in October, fully reversing the 2026Q2 surge that followed the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, with urea driving both swings.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Fertilizer prices are highly sensitive to Gulf shipping, especially urea.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s fertilizer price index

insights.claim: Fertilizer prices are projected to rise about 14 percent in 2026 and then fall 12 percent in 2027 and 8 percent in 2028 as input costs ease and non-Gulf exports increase.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Fertilizer producers' pricing tailwind fades after 2026.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s fertilizer price index

insights.claim: The metals and minerals price index is on track to rise 25 percent in 2026 to a record annual average and remain 16 percent above its 2021 peak in 2027 despite edging lower.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Base metals stay historically expensive, supportive for miners.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s metals and minerals

insights.claim: Metals demand is expected to remain firm on investment in electrification, renewable energy and data centers, while weak construction and softness in China's steel sector weigh on iron ore.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Favors electrification metals over iron ore; data centers are a named metals demand driver.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s metals and minerals

insights.claim: The precious metals index fell 7 percent in 2026Q3 after record highs, partly due to rising bond yields, tighter monetary policy and a stronger U.S. dollar, but is still projected to rise 40 percent in 2026 before falling 8 percent in 2027 and 6 percent in 2028.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Precious metals' peak may be in, with gradual declines forecast.
insights.locator: Precious metal prices eased in 2026Q3

insights.claim: Safe-haven demand and central bank gold purchases are expected to moderate but keep gold prices elevated, while silver and platinum are likely to ease as demand growth slows and supply improves.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Relative preference for gold over silver and platinum.
insights.locator: Precious metal prices eased in 2026Q3

insights.claim: For precious metals, geopolitical tensions and financial volatility are upside risks, while higher-for-longer interest rates or a stronger U.S. dollar are downside risks.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Rates and dollar are the key swing factors for precious metals.
insights.locator: The World Bank Group’s metals and minerals

insights.claim: The World Bank warns that export bans in response to high food prices can fragment markets and push global prices higher, as in 2007-08 and 2010-11.
insights.speaker: @worldbank
insights.so_what: Watch for export restrictions as an accelerant of food price spikes.
